deck-swab.context: A long-handled mop with a thick bundle of rope strands at the bottom. Used for scrubbing and washing ship decks and for marine cleaning and nautical chores.

bulbous-bow.context: Side view of a ship hull with a rounded bulb bulging forward below the waterline. Used for naval architecture, hull design and fuel efficient shipping topics.

yardarm.context: A ship mast with a long horizontal yard across it and lines running from the tips up to the masthead. Used for tall ships, rigging and old sailing vessel themes.

bowsprit.context: Front of a sailing ship with a long spar angling forward from the bow and a stay running from the mast to its tip. Used for rigging, tall ships and boat parts.

anchor-chain.context: Heavy chain of oval stud links running diagonally, each link with a bar across the middle. Used for ship anchor gear, mooring, strength and heavy duty marine hardware.

anchor-windlass.context: A deck winch with a drum and a notched wheel that pulls anchor chain up from a deck pipe. Used for raising and lowering a boat's anchor and ship deck machinery.

watertight-door.context: An oval ship door with rounded corners, a hand wheel and lever dogs around its edge. Used for bulkheads, sealed compartments, flooding protection and naval vessels.

wheelhouse.context: A small boxy cabin on a boat deck with a wide front window and a mast on its roof. Used for the pilothouse, bridge, steering station and captain's cabin of a boat.

bow-thruster.context: Ship bow seen from the side with a round tunnel through the hull and a small propeller inside. Used for maneuvering ships sideways when docking in harbours.

ducted-propeller.context: A ship propeller enclosed in a short round nozzle ring, with a rudder beside it. Used for tugboats, thrust efficiency and marine propulsion systems.

azimuth-thruster.context: A pod drive hanging below a ship hull on a vertical strut with a propeller at its front. Used for steerable ship propulsion, dynamic positioning and icebreakers.

deadeye.context: A round wooden block with three holes in a triangle and a rope lashed below it. Used for rigging and tightening shrouds on old sailing ships.

belaying-pin.context: A wooden pin shaped like a small club standing in a ship's rail, used to tie off ropes. Used for sailing ship rigging and traditional seamanship.

ratlines.context: Two slanting shroud ropes from a ship's rail to the mast, joined by short horizontal rungs like a ladder. Used for climbing a sailing ship's rigging.

draft-marks.context: Ship hull side with a vertical scale of numbers painted above the waterline. Used for reading how deep a vessel sits, loading limits and cargo weight surveys.

companionway.context: A steep narrow ladder with handrails leading down through an open deck hatch. Used for the stairs into a boat's cabin and going below deck.

gimbal-lamp.context: A lantern hung inside a swinging ring bracket so it stays upright when the boat tilts. Used for cabin lighting, oil lamps and seafaring decor.

sailboat-keel.context: Sailboat hull with a small sail, a deep narrow fin keel and a heavy bulb at its tip. Used for sailing stability, ballast and yacht design topics.

stern-gallery.context: Back end of an old sailing ship with rows of windows under a lantern on top. Used for galleons, captain's cabins and historic tall ship themes.

boat-steering-console.context: Center console of a small boat with a wheel, a throttle lever and a windscreen on top. Used for helm stations on powerboats and fishing boats.

marine-throttle.context: Boat throttle control box with a single lever angled forward on a panel. Used for engine speed and gear control on motorboats and outboards.

grapnel-anchor.context: A small anchor with a straight shank and four curved tines spread like a claw. Used for dinghies, small boats, and recovering objects from the water.

fluke-anchor.context: A flat anchor with two wide triangular flukes on a crossbar at the bottom of a shank. Used for holding boats firmly in sand and mud on the seabed.

plow-anchor.context: An anchor with a single pointed plowshare blade hinged at the end of a long shank. Used for holding boats on varied seabeds, cruising and offshore yachts.

mushroom-anchor.context: An anchor with a straight shank ending in an upside-down bowl like a mushroom cap. Used for permanent moorings and holding buoys in soft mud.

sea-anchor.context: A cone-shaped fabric drogue on bridle lines trailing underwater behind a boat. Used for slowing a boat in storms, heaving to and emergency drift control.

lateen-sail.context: A mast with a long diagonal yard carrying a large triangular sail angled across it. Used for dhows, feluccas and traditional Mediterranean and Indian Ocean sailing.

gaff-sail.context: A four-sided sail on a mast with a slanting spar along its top edge and a boom along the bottom. Used for gaff rigged cutters, schooners and classic sailboats.

square-sail.context: A rectangular sail hanging from a horizontal yard on a mast and billowing outward. Used for viking ships, tall ships and square rigged vessels.

jib-sail.context: A small triangular headsail running from the top of a forestay down to the bow, with a mast beside it. Used for sailboat parts and sail trim topics.

reefed-sail.context: A mainsail lowered partway with its bottom bundled along the boom and tied up with a row of reef ties. Used for shortening sail in strong wind and storms.

roller-furling-jib.context: A headsail rolled tightly around a forestay into a tube with a drum at the bottom, and a partly unrolled sail beside it. Used for easy sail handling on cruising yachts.

winch-handle.context: An L-shaped winch handle with a square drive plug at one end and a round grip at the other. Used to crank sheets and halyards on sailboats.

cam-cleat.context: Two spring-loaded toothed cams side by side on a base that grip a rope between them. Used for holding sheets and lines on dinghies and small sailboats.

masthead-wind-vane.context: Top of a mast with a swinging arrow vane and a crossbar showing wind direction. Used for sailing, wind direction indicators and boat instruments.

bosuns-chair.context: A sling seat hanging from rope bridle lines and a ring, used to hoist a sailor up a mast. Used for mast climbing and rigging repairs on sailboats.

boat-shoes.context: A low moccasin-style shoe seen from the side with a lace running around its top edge. Used for sailing footwear, preppy casual style and non-slip deck shoes.

boat-bailer.context: A scoop cut from a plastic jug with its handle still attached, used to bail water out of a boat. Used for bilge water, dinghy safety and leaks.

oarlock.context: A U-shaped metal fork on a pin mounted on a boat's gunwale with an oar resting in it. Used for rowing boats, dinghies and pulling oars.

windvane-steering-gear.context: An upright wind vane on a boat's stern linked to a small rudder blade in the water. Used for self steering on long offshore sailing passages.

sailing-trapeze.context: A sailor standing straight out from the side of a small dinghy, hanging from a wire on the mast. Used for racing dinghies, hiking out and balancing in strong wind.

tacking-maneuver.context: A zigzag course heading up toward a wind arrow, turning at each tack. Used for sailing upwind, beating and route planning against the wind.

kamal.context: A small rectangular board with a knotted string through its center, an old tool for measuring a star's height above the horizon. Used for historic navigation and celestial topics.

hand-bearing-compass.context: A handheld compass with a round card window on top of a pistol style grip. Used for taking bearings to landmarks from a boat.

navigation-plotter.context: A clear square plotting tool with a rotating compass rose disc in the middle. Used for laying courses and measuring bearings on paper sea charts.

distress-flare.context: A handheld cylindrical flare with a grip band and bright sparks bursting from its top. Used for signaling for help at sea and in emergencies.

ships-logbook.context: A thick bound book with an anchor on its cover. Used for recording a ship's voyage, positions, weather and events day by day.

ship-inclinometer.context: A curved scale gauge with a hanging pointer showing how far a ship is heeling to one side. Used for measuring roll, list and heel angle.

taffrail-log.context: A dial gauge with a line trailing into the water behind a ship to a small spinning rotor. Used for measuring a ship's speed and distance run.

burgee.context: A triangular pennant on a short staff at the top of a mast, flying out to the side. Used for yacht club flags and identifying a boat's club or owner.

swallowtail-burgee.context: A flag with a deep V-shaped notch cut into its fly end, forming two tails, on a short staff. Used for yacht commodore and club officer flags.

commissioning-pennant.context: A very long narrow streamer tapering to a point, flying from the top of a mast. Used for warships in commission and naval tradition.

dressed-ship.context: Side view of a ship with a line of small signal flags running from the bow up over the mast and down to the stern. Used for celebrations, regattas and ceremonies.

anchor-ball.context: The front of a boat with a single round black ball hoisted above the bow. Used for showing a vessel is anchored, from the rules of the road at sea.

motor-sailing-cone.context: A sailboat mast with a single cone shape hoisted point down in the rigging. Used for showing a sailing vessel is also running its engine, from the rules of the road.

restricted-maneuverability-shapes.context: A vertical line of three day shapes hoisted on a mast: a ball, a diamond and a ball. Used for vessels restricted in their ability to maneuver, from the rules of the road.

not-under-command-shapes.context: Two round black balls hoisted one above the other on a line from a mast. Used for showing a vessel cannot maneuver because of breakdown or damage.

buoyancy-compensator.context: An inflatable diving vest with shoulder straps, a waist strap and a hose at the left shoulder. Used for controlling buoyancy underwater while scuba diving.

dive-knife.context: A dive knife in a sheath strapped around a lower leg with two straps. Used for scuba diving safety, cutting fishing line and freeing tangled divers.

dive-light.context: A chunky underwater torch with a wide lens head, a thick body and a wrist lanyard. Used for night dives, cave diving and lighting up dark reefs.

dive-slate.context: A small writing board with a clip at the top and a pencil hanging beside it. Used for underwater notes, hand signals and communicating between scuba divers.

submersible-pressure-gauge.context: A round dial gauge in a rubber boot at the end of a high-pressure hose. Used for checking how much air is left in a scuba tank.

rebreather.context: A backpack unit with two looped breathing hoses running to a single mouthpiece. Used for closed circuit diving, technical dives and silent underwater breathing.

dive-reel.context: A spool of guideline on a frame with a pistol grip handle and a winding crank. Used for laying a line in cave and wreck diving so divers can find their way out.

full-face-dive-mask.context: A diving mask covering the whole face in one oval shape with a built-in regulator bump at the mouth. Used for scuba, commercial diving and underwater communication.

atmospheric-diving-suit.context: A bulky hard-shell diving suit with a domed viewport head, jointed limbs and pincer hands. Used for very deep dives kept at normal surface pressure.

monofin.context: A single wide tail-shaped fin with two foot pockets side by side. Used for freediving, finswimming competitions and mermaid swimming.

hookah-dive-compressor.context: A small compressor on a floating ring with a long air hose running down to a diver. Used for surface supplied air, shallow diving and hull cleaning.

underwater-habitat.context: A cylindrical seafloor laboratory on legs with round portholes and an entry shaft below. Used for saturation diving, ocean research and aquanaut missions.

diver-ok-signal.context: A diver figure with one arm curved over the top of the head. Used for the surface OK hand signal between scuba divers and for showing all is well.

longline-fishing.context: A horizontal fishing line held up by floats, with short lines hanging down that each end in a hook. Used for commercial fishing, tuna and swordfish catching and bycatch topics.

jackline-tether.context: A safety strap with a clip at each end, one on a harness ring and one hooked to a line along the deck. Used for staying attached to a boat offshore and at night.
